title: Carry a weight, then stop. Does it swing? Stop at 1 s: 18.4 degrees; stop at 2 s: it hangs still
description:
Carry a weight on a string, then stop. Does it swing? Two panels, same string, same speed, side view. A point weight hangs on a light inextensible string of length L = g (T / 2 pi)^2 = 0.993657 m (99.4 cm), so the small-swing period is T = 2.0000 s (g = 9.807 m/s^2). The hand moves along a level rail at V = 0.5 m/s from t = 0 and stops dead at t = tau: the top panel after 1.0 s (half a swing), the bottom panel after 2.0 s (one full swing). The start and the stop are instant: the weight keeps its absolute velocity, so at the start theta' = -V / L in the hand's frame and at the stop theta' jumps by +V cos(theta) / L while the string's impulse kills the radial part V sin(theta). Between the jumps the weight is a plain pendulum, L theta'' = -g sin(theta), integrated by RK4 at 10000 steps per second with compensated summation and an energy check; after the stop it swings about the fixed hand with amplitude acos(1 - E / (g L)). Linear check: the residual swing is 2 (V / (omega L)) |sin(pi tau / T)|, twice the carrying swing at tau = T / 2 and zero at tau = T. Shown at 1/2 speed on a 10 s cycle, 4 runs in 40 s. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- the move: the weight starts at theta' = -0.5032 rad/s in the hand's frame and swings 9.187 degrees (linear 9.177; RK4 peak 9.187), 15.9 cm behind the hand at the far point; the nonlinear period at 9.187 degrees is 2.0032 s (the RK4 table crosses zero at 1.0016 s and 2.0032 s); tension 0.9872 g to 1.0257 g
- stop at 1.0 s (top panel): the hand has moved 0.500 m; the weight is at -0.046 degrees moving at +0.5032 rad/s in the hand's frame (1.0000 m/s over the ground); the string kills a radial speed of -0.00040 m/s and theta' becomes +1.0064 rad/s; the residual swing is 18.434 degrees (linear 18.354), 2.006 times the carrying swing, 31.4 cm each way and 5.10 cm up; least tension 0.949 g
- stop at 2.0 s (bottom panel): the hand has moved 1.000 m; the weight is at +0.093 degrees moving at -0.5032 rad/s (0.0000 m/s over the ground); the string kills +0.00081 m/s and theta' becomes +0.0000 rad/s; the residual swing is 0.093 degrees (linear 0.000), 0.16 cm of sideways motion: it hangs still; least tension 0.987 g
- the two residuals differ by a factor of 198.7; the stop at 2.0 s leaves 0.093 degrees because the nonlinear period is 2.0032 s, not 2.0000 s: the exact zero of the residual is at tau = 2.0032 s, where 0.000 degrees are left
- energy drift below 1.2e-15 J/kg; a half-step rerun gives 18.4335732 and 0.0927903 degrees, +0.0e+00 against the full step
- top panel (angle from the plumb line, positive ahead): 0.5 s -9.19 deg, 1.0 s -0.05 deg (the stop), 1.5 s +18.43 deg, 2.5 s -18.42 deg; bottom panel: 1.5 s +9.19 deg, 2.0 s +0.09 deg (the stop), 2.5 s +0.00 deg, 3.0 s -0.09 deg
- stops at 0.5 s and 1.5 s: 12.906 and 12.972 degrees (linear 12.978), least tension 0.975 and 0.974 g, reach 22.2 and 22.3 cm
- at 1 m/s on the same string: 18.43 degrees during the move (nonlinear period 2.0130 s); a stop at 1 s leaves 37.36 degrees (linear 36.71; least tension 0.795 g; reach 60.3 cm) and a stop at 2 s leaves 0.75 degrees (1.3 cm); its exact zero is at 2.0130 s
- a hand that ramps up over 0.1 s and down over 0.1 s instead of jumping: 18.35 and 0.092 degrees; with 0.3 s ramps: 17.73 and 0.080 degrees
- a 10 m crane cable (T = 6.345 s) carried at 1 m/s: the load swings 5.79 degrees during the move; a stop after half a swing at 3.172 s leaves 11.59 degrees (201 cm each way) and a stop after one swing at 6.345 s leaves 0.023 degrees
- a 1.00 m string (T = 2.0064 s) at 0.5 m/s: stops at 1 and 2 s leave 18.37 and 0.27 degrees; a stop at its own period 2.0064 s leaves 0.092 degrees

Why: carried at a steady speed, the weight is a pendulum in the hand's frame that starts with a kick of V backwards, so it swings 9.2 degrees about the moving hand with a period of two seconds. Half a swing after the start it passes under the hand moving forward at V relative to the hand. Stop then and the hand's V is taken away: relative to the fixed hand the weight now moves at twice V, so it swings twice as far, 18.4 degrees. One full swing after the start it passes under the hand moving backwards at V relative to the hand, so it is standing still over the ground. Stop then and the hand joins it at rest: all that is left is the 0.093 degrees that the slightly longer nonlinear period leaves. Crane operators and waiters do this by feel.

Rerun sims/carrystop/carrystop.py with projects/carrystop/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
